label: Teltonika OTD140
description: Outdoor 4G Cat 4 router: 2x 100 Mbps ETH ports, 802.3af/at PoE in on the left port and 15 W of 802.3af Mode B PoE out on the right one (21 W max at the inlet, 6 W of it the router).

poe.note: 15 W, the vendor's stated maximum on the single outlet. Flyer v1.8 (2024): "PoE Out: 802.3af (42.5 - 57 VDC, max 15W) Alternative B" and "Powering options (PoE In) RJ45, PoE In: 802.3af/at (42.5 - 57 VDC, max 21W)". The 15 W is conditional on the supply: the same box draws "Idle: < 2.5 W / Max: < 6 W / PoE Max < 21 W", and 6 + 15 is the 21 W inlet ceiling, so a 21 W PoE+ source is what makes the full output available. The outlet is 802.3af Alternative B, DC on the spare pairs - pins 4/5 positive, 7/8 negative - per the pinout at https://wiki.teltonika-networks.com/view/OTD140_Powering_Options. REVISION DRIFT: flyer and datasheet v1.6 printed "PoE Out: 802.3af/at ... max 24W"; v1.8, the current revision, prints 802.3af and 15 W, so the older 24 W figure and the 802.3at class this entry used to carry are not modelled.

notes:
Read 2026-11-21 from Teltonika material. PORT CENSUS - flyer v1.8 (2024), https://download.kamami.pl/p1207980-otd140-flyer-2024-v18.pdf (200, application/pdf, 967,315 B, text layer): "Ethernet 2 x RJ45 ports, 10/100 Mbps: 2 x ETH ports (can be configured as WAN)", "Powering options (PoE In) RJ45, PoE In: 802.3af/at (42.5 - 57 VDC, max 21W)", "PoE Out: 802.3af (42.5 - 57 VDC, max 15W) Alternative B", "Power consumption Idle: < 2.5 W / Max: < 6 W / PoE Max < 21 W". https://wiki.teltonika-networks.com/view/OTD140_Powering_Options (200, 57,164 B) states the standard per direction: "OTD140 devices support active PoE standard: 802.3af/at for the PD (Powered Device) port and 802.3af standard for the PSE (Power Source Equipment) port", "Working voltage levels: 42.5-57.0 V", plus the Mode B pinout (DC+ on 4/5, DC- on 7/8). https://wiki.teltonika-networks.com/view/OTD140_Interfaces (200) confirms "2 x RJ45 ethernet ports", "2 x SIM slot", "4G LTE Cat 4".

WHAT WAS WRONG - the entry declared eth1 poeIn 12.95 (the 802.3af class ceiling) on a port the vendor rates 802.3af/at with a 21 W inlet, and eth2 poeOut true with poeOutClass "PoE+" (802.3at), which the vendor does not claim for the outlet: the PSE port is 802.3af, 15 W. With only the boolean, poeDraw() billed the outlet 1 W and show power inline could not say what the box could supply.

WHAT IT IS NOW - eth1 sinks 21 W (the vendor's "max 21W" inlet, the same number as the "PoE Max < 21 W" consumption row); eth2 sources 15 W classed 802.3af, and the poe block carries the 15 W so the ceiling is a document rather than an inference. The two are consistent by construction: 21 W in, 6 W of router, 15 W out.

NOT MODELLED - the "power supply unit dependent" condition. The catalogue has no field for "this outlet reaches 15 W only if the upstream PSE can deliver 21 W"; a lab feeding eth1 from a 15.4 W 802.3af port will see eth2 allocate its full 15 W where the real box would have about 9 W left. The < 2.5 W idle draw is also not modelled, and the second SIM slot, the UART pads and the reset button are not ports.
